concept.name: Hard stop
concept.definition: A stop-loss instruction resting with the broker or exchange as an actual order (stop or stop-limit), which triggers automatically when price reaches the stop level. It enforces the invalidation point mechanically, removing real-time discretion - at the cost of possible slippage or non-fill in fast markets.
concept.intuition: A hard stop is the exit decision executed by the machine, so the future, emotional version of you does not get a vote.
concept.mechanics: A sell-stop sits below the market (a buy-stop above it, for shorts); when the stop price trades, a stop order becomes a market order - execution guaranteed, price not - while a stop-limit becomes a limit order - price capped, execution not. Trailing-stop variants ratchet the stop with favorable price movement.
concept.failure_modes: In gaps and fast markets a stop-market fills far through the stop price, and a stop-limit may not fill at all; obvious stop levels can be run by short-term liquidity hunts before the move resumes. A hard stop does not cap gap risk.
concept.misconceptions: A stop-loss does not guarantee the exit price - 'stop' is a trigger, not a fill price. Nor are hard stops only for the undisciplined; they are structural risk control that survives distraction, outages, and emotional episodes.
concept.example: Long 250 shares at 50 with a sell-stop at 48 (planned -$500 risk); an overnight gap opens at 47.20 and the stop market-fills at 47.25 - more than planned, but bounded and automatic.
